title: getScanResults and exportScanResults leak cross-org scan data via an unscoped findById fallback
description: Confirmed live defect (CLOUD_POSTURE_BUGS_FOUND.csv #1): both getScanResults and exportScanResults (scan.controller.js) fall back to CloudPostureScan.findById(scanId) with no organizationId check when the org-scoped lookup misses, unlike getScanProgress which re-checks scan.organizationId===req.orgId after the same fallback pattern.
preconditions: Two orgs (A, B), org B has a completed scan with findings
Valid JWT for a user in org A who does not have access to org B's project
steps: As an org A user, call GET /cloud-posture/scans/:scanId/results using org B's scanId
As an org A user, call the export endpoint for the same org B scanId
expectedResult: Both requests must be rejected with 403/404 and return no scan results or export data belonging to org B. (Currently reproduces the bug: the unscoped findById fallback returns org B's data.)

title: Resource list and provider-summary endpoints trust the orgId URL path param instead of the authenticated req.orgId
description: Confirmed live defect (BUGS_FOUND.csv #12): resource.controller.js destructures { orgId, projectId } directly from req.params in getProjectResources (line ~207) and getCloudProviderResources (line ~242), and builds every Mongo filter from that path value. Route middleware only validates requireProjectMembership() against req.orgId — it never asserts req.params.orgId === req.orgId.
preconditions: User belongs to org A and has an authorized project P (also under org A)
Org B exists with its own project and cloud resources
steps: As the org A user (authenticated, valid JWT for org A), call GET /api/client/cloud-posture/organizations/:orgId/projects/:projectId/providers/:provider/dashboard with :orgId replaced by org B's ID while :projectId stays a project the caller is otherwise entitled to reach
Observe whether the request is rejected before reaching the data query
expectedResult: Request must be rejected with 403 as soon as req.params.orgId diverges from the authenticated req.orgId. (Currently reproduces the bug: filters are built from the path param, so mismatched IDs are not independently rejected by the query layer.)

title: controlScan rejects a cancel request whose scan does not belong to the caller's organization
description: Positive control, contrasted with CLPO-SEC-001/002: controlScan (scan.controller.js:861) explicitly re-checks scan.organizationId.toString() !== req.orgId?.toString() and returns 403, in addition to the org-scoped findOne filter. Regression guard to keep this path from regressing to the same unscoped-fallback pattern seen elsewhere.
preconditions: Org B has a scan currently in status 'running'
Valid JWT for a user in org A
steps: As an org A user, call POST /cloud-posture/scans/:scanId/control with {operation:'cancel'} using org B's running scanId
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403; org B's scan status remains 'running' and is unaffected by the attempted cancel.

title: A failed or interrupted connection test never leaves a readable staged credential secret in Vault
description: config.controller.js stages raw provider credentials to a per-operation Vault path before calling Prowler's validate endpoint, then destroys it in a finally block (lines ~212-218) regardless of success/failure/timeout. If this cleanup path regressed, raw AWS/GCP/Azure secrets could persist at a predictable Vault path after a single failed test.
preconditions: Ability to inspect the Vault path used for staged test-connection credentials (test/staging environment only)
steps: Submit a 'Test Connection' request for AWS with any credential values
Regardless of whether the test call succeeds, fails, or times out at 15s, immediately query Vault for the per-operation staging path used
expectedResult: The staged secret path returns not-found in every outcome (success, failure, and timeout) — the finally-block cleanup runs unconditionally and no raw credential is left recoverable in Vault.

title: Configuration endpoint rejects an unsupported provider name such as 'kubernetes' instead of silently accepting it
description: No Kubernetes credential path exists anywhere in the backend (no VAULT_FIELDS_BY_PROVIDER entry, no config sub-schema, no controller branch) despite Prowler's scan engine supporting Kubernetes. Verifies the API fails closed for unrecognized provider values rather than accepting and partially persisting them.
steps: Call PUT /api/cloud-posture-config/:projectId with provider='kubernetes' and an arbitrary credentials payload
expectedResult: Request is rejected with a 400-class error identifying the provider as unsupported; no providers.kubernetes field is created on the CloudPostureConfig document.

title: Test-connection endpoint requires membership on the target project, not just any valid org session
description: Guards against a user who is authenticated in an org but not assigned to a specific project using that project's projectId to trigger credential-validation calls (which reach live cloud provider APIs and Prowler) against a project they have no membership on.
preconditions: User X belongs to org A but is not a member of project P (also under org A)
steps: As user X, call POST /api/cloud-posture-config/test-connection with projectId=P's ID
expectedResult: Request is rejected with 403 for lack of project membership; no call is made to Prowler's credential-validate endpoint on user X's behalf.
